title: CLAUDE.md
text: epitargets R package Economic Policy Institute provides utilities targets pipeline framework. wraps targets tarchetypes add automatic date-tracking alongside pipeline targets age-based cue support API targets. General R package development conventions (workflows, documentation, testing) live .claude/rules/r_package.md. Note devtools::build_readme() also run changes affect README.Rmd.

title: CLAUDE.md
text: package code lives R/functions.R. functions fall groups: Date-tracking targets: tar_target_date() — wraps tar_target_raw() create primary target plus companion _date target records Sys.Date() primary target runs tar_age_date() — like tar_target_date() adds age-based cue via tarchetypes::tar_cue_age_raw() target re-runs configurable time period (default: 1 day) collect_target_date() — gathers _date targets tibble columns name time File read/write helpers: tar_csv_read() — creates pair targets: _file target tracking CSV path (format = "file") read target using readr::read_csv() tar_parquet_read() — like tar_csv_read() reads via arrow::read_parquet(); read target defaults format = "parquet" create_csv() — thin wrapper around readr::write_csv() returns file path (useful targets format function) Interactive helpers: tar_read_stash() — reads target via targets::tar_read_raw() assigns value environment (default .target global env) interactive exploration rstudio_addin_tar_read_stash() — RStudio/Positron addin stashes target named cursor via tar_read_stash(), using atcursor (optional dependency) locate symbol

text: code uses functions targets, tarchetypes (tar_cue_age_raw), readr (read_csv, write_csv), arrow (read_parquet), tibble (tibble), rlang. atcursor optional (Suggests) dependency used RStudio addin.

title: Economic Policy Institute tools for working with targets
text: tar_target_date() drop-replacement targets::tar_target(). creates target plus companion _date target records ran:
code: targets::tar_dir({   targets::tar_script({     library(epitargets)     list(       tar_target_date(wages, data.frame(year = 2020:2024, wage = c(15, 15, 16, 17, 18)))     )   })   targets::tar_make()   print(targets::tar_read(wages))   print(targets::tar_read(wages_date)) }) #> + wages dispatched #> ✔ wages completed [0ms, 191 B] #> + wages_date dispatched #> ✔ wages_date completed [0ms, 81 B] #> ✔ ended pipeline [124ms, 2 completed, 0 skipped] #>   year wage #> 1 2020   15 #> 2 2021   15 #> 3 2022   16 #> 4 2023   17 #> 5 2024   18 #> [1] "2026-07-04"

title: Economic Policy Institute tools for working with targets
text: tar_age_date() adds age-based cue target automatically re-runs time period. Useful API calls data goes stale:
code: targets::tar_dir({   targets::tar_script({     library(epitargets)     list(       tar_age_date(daily_data, Sys.time(), age = as.difftime(1, units = "days"))     )   })   targets::tar_make()   print(targets::tar_read(daily_data))   print(targets::tar_read(daily_data_date)) }) #> + daily_data dispatched #> ✔ daily_data completed [0ms, 96 B] #> + daily_data_date dispatched #> ✔ daily_data_date completed [0ms, 81 B] #> ✔ ended pipeline [127ms, 2 completed, 0 skipped] #> [1] "2026-07-04 15:41:27 EDT" #> [1] "2026-07-04"

title: Economic Policy Institute tools for working with targets
text: collect_target_date() gathers _date targets single tibble can see glance target last ran:
code: targets::tar_dir({   targets::tar_script({     library(epitargets)     list(       tar_target_date(wages, data.frame(wage = 18)),       tar_age_date(prices, data.frame(price = 3.50)),       targets::tar_target(freshness, collect_target_date(wages_date, prices_date))     )   })   targets::tar_make()   targets::tar_read(freshness) }) #> + prices dispatched #> ✔ prices completed [1ms, 118 B] #> + wages dispatched #> ✔ wages completed [1ms, 118 B] #> + prices_date dispatched #> ✔ prices_date completed [0ms, 81 B] #> + wages_date dispatched #> ✔ wages_date completed [0ms, 81 B] #> + freshness dispatched #> ✔ freshness completed [2ms, 179 B] #> ✔ ended pipeline [148ms, 5 completed, 0 skipped] #> # A tibble: 2 × 2 #>   name   time       #>   <chr>  <date>     #> 1 wages  2026-07-04 #> 2 prices 2026-07-04
